key_insight: The paper introduces GATE, a graph-decomposition framework that jointly designs agreement constraints, dual variables, and cooperative subgraph computations to turn decentralized optimization into message passing over trees.
engineering_relevance: It provides a principled way to build faster and more scalable decentralized optimizers whose communication and computation are matched to the network topology.
method: Represent consensus with one variable per edge and decompose the graph into tree blocks.
Update edge variables by minimizing the sum of endpoint cost-to-go messages, then relax the result.
Use tree-recursive message updates; GATE-S replaces exact subproblems with surrogate local models and lightweight messages.
evidence_signal: The authors report linear convergence with a rate that explicitly depends on function regularity, network topology, and the chosen graph partition, and they validate performance with numerical experiments.
watch_item: Performance and implementation efficiency depend on the quality of the graph partition and the cost of computing/approximating tree messages.
paper_title: From Mixing to Tearing: Graph Decomposition in Decentralized Optimization via Message Passing
